value.rationale: Two narrow observation windows are a natural limiting geometry for stable recovery of finite-band Fourier signals. The theorem determines the sharp worst-case energy exponent and exact all-bandwidth constant, proves uniquely optimal macroscopic window separation including moving geometries, and quantifies spectral conditioning. It goes beyond a generic scaling or a sample-grid computation; one can use the precise constants when comparing sensor layouts and bandwidth penalties. The fixed-band limit and exact m=1 optimization are carefully distinguished.
